arrays.title: Arrays: operations, storage, and interview patterns
arrays.description: Understand array indexing, insertion, iteration, and resizing, then practice the invariants used in array and matrix interview problems.

implement-an-array.title: Implement an array data structure
implement-an-array.description: Build an array abstraction and reason about indexed access, insertion, removal, capacity, and the costs of moving existing elements.

walk-a-matrix.title: Walk a matrix: two-dimensional array traversal
walk-a-matrix.description: Practice traversing a two-dimensional matrix while tracking row and column boundaries and handling small or empty inputs.

product-array.title: Product of Array Except Self: prefix and suffix products
product-array.description: Compute each array position from the product of the other values without division. Work through prefix/suffix state and zero-value cases.

valid-sudoku-board.title: Validate a Sudoku board with sets
valid-sudoku-board.description: Check Sudoku rows, columns, and subgrids for duplicate values. Practice mapping board positions to the constraints they must satisfy.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock: one-pass reasoning
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.description: Find the best single buy-and-sell opportunity by tracking an earlier minimum. Practice ordering constraints and decreasing-price inputs.

big-o-time-and-space-complexity.title: Big O notation: time and space complexity
big-o-time-and-space-complexity.description: Analyze how interview solutions grow with input size. Compare loops, recursion, auxiliary memory, and common complexity classes.

hash-tables.title: Hash tables: lookups, collisions, and frequency counts
hash-tables.description: Learn how hashing maps keys to storage, why collisions matter, and how maps and sets support common interview optimizations.

implement-a-hash-table.title: Implement a hash table and handle collisions
implement-a-hash-table.description: Build a hash-table implementation, store and retrieve key/value pairs, and examine how collisions affect correctness and performance.

catch-the-hacker.title: Find the most frequent value with a hash map
catch-the-hacker.description: Identify a repeatedly duplicated email by counting frequencies. Compare repeated scans with a map-based pass through the input.

target-two-sum.title: Two Sum: complement lookup and distinct indices
target-two-sum.description: Find two distinct indices whose values reach a target. Compare pair enumeration with a hash-map solution and test duplicate values.

strings.title: Strings for interviews: representation and operations
strings.description: Study string traversal, character representation, immutability, and construction costs before practicing text interview problems.

palindromes-permutataions-anagrams.title: Palindromes, permutations, and anagrams explained
palindromes-permutataions-anagrams.description: Distinguish palindrome order, permutation arrangements, and anagram frequency counts, then choose the state each text problem needs.

group-permutations-of-palindromes.title: Group permutations of palindromes
group-permutations-of-palindromes.description: Practice grouping strings by character relationships and reasoning about which arrangements can form a palindrome.

recursion.title: Recursion: base cases, call stacks, and return values
recursion.description: Trace recursive execution, define a smaller subproblem, and connect base cases and return values to a clear correctness argument.

sum-digits.title: Sum the digits of a number without converting to a string
sum-digits.description: Compute a number’s digit sum using arithmetic. Practice recursive decomposition, termination, and tests for single-digit inputs.

generate-all-permutations.title: Generate all permutations with backtracking
generate-all-permutations.description: Enumerate input arrangements while managing choices and restoring state. Analyze the output size and test small permutation examples.

logarithms-and-time-complexity.title: Logarithms and logarithmic time complexity
logarithms-and-time-complexity.description: Understand why repeated halving produces logarithmic work and apply that reasoning to search intervals and recursive algorithms.

searching-and-binary-search.title: Binary search: sorted input and interval invariants
searching-and-binary-search.description: Search sorted data by narrowing a candidate interval. Practice boundaries, midpoint updates, and the conditions that guarantee progress.

sorting.title: Sorting algorithms and interview tradeoffs
sorting.description: Compare sorting approaches, runtime assumptions, and the ways sorted order changes an interview problem’s available solutions.

interview-scheduler.title: Interview Scheduler: searching for an available time
interview-scheduler.description: Work through an interview scheduling problem and practice using ordered information to reduce the search for a valid answer.

shifted-search.title: Search a rotated sorted array
shifted-search.description: Find a target in a shifted sorted array by reasoning about ordered intervals and choosing which half can still contain the answer.

sorted-matrix-search.title: Search a sorted matrix
sorted-matrix-search.description: Use a matrix’s ordering constraints to reduce the search space. Track boundaries and test targets at edges or outside the data.

age-sort.title: Age Sort: use bounded values to organize an array
age-sort.description: Explore how a restricted value range can change a sorting problem. Compare counting-based work with general comparison sorting.

first-bad-version.title: First Bad Version: binary search on a boundary
first-bad-version.description: Find a transition in an ordered sequence using a predicate. Practice binary-search interval definitions and edge-boundary cases.

linked-lists.title: Linked lists: nodes, links, and traversal
linked-lists.description: Understand linked-list structure, traversal costs, and the pointer relationships behind insertion, deletion, and reversal.

pointers.title: Pointers and references in linked structures
pointers.description: Reason about references, node identity, and reachability so pointer updates do not lose the remainder of a list or tree.

implement-a-linked-list.title: Implement a linked list
implement-a-linked-list.description: Build linked nodes and list operations, maintain head and tail relationships, and test empty and single-node structures.

combine-blockchains.title: Combine Blockchains: work with linked chains
combine-blockchains.description: Practice combining linked chains while preserving their nodes and maintaining the relationships needed to traverse the result.

reverse-a-linked-list.title: Reverse a linked list: preserve and redirect pointers
reverse-a-linked-list.description: Reverse a list by tracking the previous, current, and next nodes. Explain the invariant and handle empty and single-node inputs.

mirror-delete.title: Mirror Delete: linked-list removal practice
mirror-delete.description: Work through a linked-list deletion exercise with careful reference updates, boundary checks, and tests that preserve reachable nodes.

queues.title: Queues: first-in-first-out processing
queues.description: Learn queue operations, implementation choices, and the role of first-in-first-out order in breadth-first traversal and scheduling.

stacks.title: Stacks: last-in-first-out processing
stacks.description: Learn stack operations and use last-in-first-out state for nested structures, traversal, and interview problem solving.

implement-a-queue.title: Implement a queue data structure
implement-a-queue.description: Implement enqueue and dequeue behavior while maintaining first-in-first-out order and handling empty-queue transitions.

implement-a-stack.title: Implement a stack data structure
implement-a-stack.description: Implement push, pop, and peek, maintain the top of the stack, and reason about operation costs and empty-state behavior.

max-min-stack.title: Min and max stack: retain aggregate state
max-min-stack.description: Support stack operations while tracking minimum and maximum values. Practice duplicate values and restoring earlier aggregate state.

valid-brackets.title: Valid brackets: match nested delimiters with a stack
valid-brackets.description: Validate bracket ordering with a stack of unmatched openings. Test mismatched types, unfinished openings, and closing-first inputs.

trees.title: Trees: structure, height, and recursive reasoning
trees.description: Learn tree terminology and recursive structure, then prepare for traversal, depth, ancestor, and binary-search-tree exercises.

tree-traversal-in-order-pre-order-post-o.title: Binary tree traversal: inorder, preorder, and postorder
tree-traversal-in-order-pre-order-post-o.description: Compare traversal orders by changing when each node is processed. Trace recursive calls and distinguish traversal from search-tree ordering.

binary-search-trees.title: Binary search trees: ordering and search
binary-search-trees.description: Understand the ordering rules that guide binary-search-tree operations and how tree height affects search performance.

implement-a-binary-search-tree.title: Implement a binary search tree
implement-a-binary-search-tree.description: Build a binary search tree, preserve its ordering contract during updates, and test search paths and empty-tree behavior.

binary-tree-max-depth.title: Maximum depth of a binary tree
binary-tree-max-depth.description: Compute a tree’s depth from its subtrees. State the empty-tree convention and compare balanced and chain-shaped inputs.

binary-search-tree-validate.title: Validate a binary search tree with ancestor bounds
binary-search-tree-validate.description: Check the complete binary-search-tree ordering rule, including ancestor constraints that a parent-only comparison can miss.

closest-common-ancestor-in-binary-tree.title: Lowest common ancestor of a binary tree
closest-common-ancestor-in-binary-tree.description: Find the shared ancestor of two nodes by reasoning about subtree results and the relationship between node identity and ancestry.

graphs.title: Graphs: representations, traversal, and interview problems
graphs.description: Model relationships with graph nodes and edges, compare representations, and prepare for reachability and traversal exercises.

depth-first-search.title: Depth-first search: visited state and active paths
depth-first-search.description: Traverse a graph by following branches, track visited nodes to handle cycles, and reason about recursive or explicit stack state.

breadth-first-search.title: Breadth-first search: queues and shortest unweighted paths
breadth-first-search.description: Traverse by distance with a queue, avoid duplicate discoveries, and reconstruct shortest paths when edges have equal cost.

implement-a-graph.title: Implement a graph data structure
implement-a-graph.description: Represent vertices and edges, maintain neighbor relationships, and prepare a graph structure for traversal and reachability queries.

pilot-a-rocket.title: Shortest path in an unweighted graph: Pilot a Rocket
pilot-a-rocket.description: Find a route through a satellite network. Practice BFS discovery order, parent tracking, cycles, and an unreachable destination.

count-islands.title: Number of Islands: DFS and BFS region counting
count-islands.description: Count connected land regions in a matrix. Compare DFS and BFS, mark visited cells, and test disconnected and diagonal land.

robot-maze.title: Robot Maze: find a valid path through a grid
robot-maze.description: Determine whether a robot can reach an exit under the allowed movement rules. Practice grid bounds, blocked cells, and path choices.

subproblems-and-overlapping-subproblems.title: Subproblems and overlapping subproblems
subproblems-and-overlapping-subproblems.description: Identify repeated smaller decisions and define state precisely before using caching or a dynamic-programming table.

memoization.title: Memoization: cache repeated subproblem results
memoization.description: Turn repeated recursive work into reusable results. Choose complete cache keys and distinguish missing results from valid zero values.

bottom-up-vs-top-down.title: Top-down vs. bottom-up dynamic programming
bottom-up-vs-top-down.description: Compare memoized recursion with tabulation, choose a valid evaluation order, and reason about stack and table storage.

dynamic-programming.title: Dynamic programming: states, transitions, and subproblems
dynamic-programming.description: Develop a recurrence, identify repeated states, and connect memoization and tabulation to interview problem-solving strategies.

vending-machine.title: Vending Machine: dynamic programming practice
vending-machine.description: Work through a vending-machine interview problem by identifying choices, smaller subproblems, and the state needed to reuse results.

three-moves.title: Three Moves: dynamic programming practice
three-moves.description: Define transitions for a constrained-movement problem and practice solving repeated subproblems without recomputing each path.

steal-packages.title: House Robber: choose non-adjacent values with dynamic programming
steal-packages.description: Maximize a total without taking adjacent entries. Derive skip/take decisions and compare recursive, memoized, and iterative approaches.

why-does-javascript-get-its-own-topic.title: Why JavaScript interview preparation needs language practice
why-does-javascript-get-its-own-topic.description: Connect general algorithm skills with JavaScript-specific behavior, browser programming, and practical utility implementations.

javascript-interview-questions.title: JavaScript interview questions and language concepts
javascript-interview-questions.description: Practice explaining JavaScript behavior and implementation choices alongside algorithm exercises and practical coding questions.

fix-this.title: JavaScript this binding: fix the receiver
fix-this.description: Trace JavaScript receivers and callback invocation so you can explain and repair unexpected this values in interview code.

array-methods.title: Implement JavaScript array methods
array-methods.description: Practice array-method behavior, callback arguments, iteration, and edge cases by implementing familiar JavaScript operations.

build-a-javascript-promise.title: Build a JavaScript Promise implementation
build-a-javascript-promise.description: Explore asynchronous state, fulfillment, rejection, and chaining by building a teaching implementation of promise behavior.

pub-sub-and-event-driven-programming.title: Build a JavaScript pub-sub and event emitter
pub-sub-and-event-driven-programming.description: Implement event subscription and publication, track listeners, and connect the pattern to event-driven JavaScript applications.

debounce.title: Debounce in JavaScript: implementation and timing
debounce.description: Implement a debounce that waits for activity to settle. Trace timers, preserve arguments and this, and compare it with throttling.

throttle.title: Throttle in JavaScript: implementation and timing
throttle.description: Limit callback frequency during repeated events. Explain cooldown windows, trailing updates, and how throttling differs from debounce.
